newsitem.title: UGANDA: African ministers keep sanctions against Burundi.
newsitem.headline: African ministers keep sanctions against Burundi.

text.p: African foreign ministers meeting in Kampala have agreed that economic sanctions imposed against Burundi last year, in protest against a military coup there, should remain in force.

Tanzanian Foreign Affairs Minister Jakaya Kikwete told reporters on Saturday night: "The sanctions have had some success. They have forced (Burundi President Pierre) Buyoya to restore the parliament, although it is not meeting at present.
"But the sanctions must continue until they achieve their objective of restoring democratic rule," Kikwete said.
He said the meeting had called on countries which have relaxed sanctions to restore them. He did not name the countries.
Regional countries led by Tanzania slapped sanctions on Burundi on July 31 last year after Tutsi military strongman Buyoya ousted Hutu civilian president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya.

The ministers recommended that a summit meeting of African presidents should be called to study the Burundi situation. This would follow talks with Burundi political parties scheduled for August 25 in Arusha, Tanzania.
The Kampala meeting was attended by ministers from Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia and Zimbabwe.
